source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CloudHQ's LC8 campus in Ashburn publishes 756 MW of IT capacity, the largest disclosed power figure for any Virginia data center.

The scale is real but the disclosure is selective. Only 29 of the 376 mapped Virginia facilities publish a megawatt figure at all, and this one site accounts for roughly 29 percent of the 2,563.4 MW those 29 facilities report. A single campus holding that share of published capacity says as much about who chooses to disclose as about who builds the most.

The density is what ties this to AI. At 850,000 square feet of technical space, 756 MW works out to about 889 watts per square foot, well above a conventional enterprise data center and consistent with dense compute. Converting that load to racks requires an assumption the operator does not publish: at 40 kW per rack the campus is roughly 18,900 racks, at 100 kW per rack roughly 7,560. Neither figure is CloudHQ's claim, and the accelerator count depends on chips per rack, which is also unpublished.

What the data does not cover matters here. There are no certifications listed, so nothing indicates what workloads the campus is qualified to host. There is no announced expansion in the record. And 756 MW of published IT capacity is not 756 MW delivered: the grid connection behind it determines when, or whether, the capacity becomes usable.
